transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-20
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Parkview CTO), Sofia Martinez (Head of Infra), David Kim (Security Lead), Rina Patel (SRE)
Links shared: runbook draft: https://drive.example.com/parkview-runbook-draft.pdf, bench sheet: https://sheets.example.com/pv-pilot-bench

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call — I see Liam, Sofia, David, Rina, and Priya. Can folks confirm audio?
[00:12] Liam: Yep, loud and clear. Sorry running between meetings, but I'm here.
[00:15] Sofia: here, audio ok.
[00:18] David: here.
[00:22] Jordan: Sweet, agenda for today: connectivity verification, runbook updates, kernel/quant tuning plan, and quick telemetry check. Priya, want to take first on the runbook changes?
[00:30] Priya: Yeah, sure. I pushed an updated PDF to the drive, it's got the canary routing flow and the specific NLB healthcheck payloads. A couple of notes — we noticed the healthcheck interval defaults to 10s on Parkview side which made the canary too slow to failover in the test, so we recommended 5s with a 3-fail threshold. I also added curl examples for the readiness probes.
[01:05] Sofia: Quick question — those healthchecks, are they HTTP 200s against the front door, or TCP level? We have some legacy TCP probes for internal NLB.
[01:12] Priya: Right now the doc has HTTP 200 checks hitting /_ready on the gateway. If you must keep TCP we can provide a TCP probe example, but the body-based readiness lets us validate model runtime warm states (KV cache primed).
[01:30] Liam: KV cache? I thought you had a separate prefix cache on the private runtime — just want to understand warm vs cold behavior and how that interacts with our sticky sessions.
[01:40] Priya: Yeah, sorry. The cache we mean is the KV cache — key-value token cache we keep per conversational session. On cold-starts you'll see higher latencies until it's warmed. That's why we instrument the readiness so the node only marks healthy once cache has hit a minimal warm threshold. Some of our earlier tests reported a lot of cold-starts when connection churn hit the NAT.
[02:05] Rina: On the NAT point, we saw ephemeral source IPs for some worker pods behind our N A T gateway which broke session affinity. We're running an AWS NATGW plus an internal Egress LB; we've got a note in the sheet.
[02:20] Jordan: Right — that ties to the 'egress IP sticky' recommendation in the runbook. Sofia, can you confirm what you want as TTL for DNS and the source IP setup?
[02:32] Sofia: We're standard at 60s for the app DNS TTL. For egress, we can reserve an elastic IP pool for the Redwood private nodes, but coil wants to keep the NATGW for cost. Might need a small change to route table to preserve source IP.
[02:48] Priya: OK, in that scenario we recommend either a NAT with source preservation or we use the outbound static egress mapping on our side — we call that 'egress pinning' in the doc. If you keep NATGW, you'll need to configure the SNAT to keep the same public IP for a session window; otherwise the runtime will see new source IPs and drop the session mapping which is what caused the KV mismatch.
[03:15] Liam: Got it. And what about fallback routing? If a node fails, how fast will traffic go to the hosted fallback?
[03:23] Priya: Our default fallback policy in the pilot is 5s for healthcheck notice, plus immediate reroute to a warm hosted pool in the nearest region. There's a 2-step failover: first try another private node in the same cluster, then fall back to hosted. That was configurable in the canary config we sent.
[03:45] Jordan: Quick interjection — Parkview asked earlier about cost tradeoffs: if you lean on hosted fallback more, that increases token costs vs dedicated capacity but keeps latency lower than keeping a cold private pool. We'll include a table in the pricing appendix.
[03:58] Liam: Makes sense. We're mostly evaluating behavior under steady load and also under a surge scenario from our ingestion pipeline.
[04:10] Rina: We did a surge sim yesterday — 20% of requests spiked in 10 seconds — and observed about 120ms extra p95 on generator requests and some 5xxs during the short window. Logged here: bench sheet.
[04:26] Priya: Do you have the logs where the NAT mapping changed during that spike? The 5xx often lines up with the session rewrite.
[04:33] Rina: yes, I'll paste the snippet after the call.
[04:37] David: From a security front, quick note — our audit team wants full request IDs to be logged and correlated with KMS key use. Priya, you said Redwood supports HSM-backed keys?
[04:46] Priya: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS in the private deployment. It's the same flow, we just integrate the key policy and we don't persist cleartext. We'll send the key policy template.
[04:55] David: Great. Also need to confirm retention on logs and SSO mapping for RBAC.
[04:59] Jordan: We'll attach the SOC2 and audit checklist; I think Priya flagged the RBAC SAML mapping doc in the shared folder.
[05:07] Priya: Yup, doc's there.
[05:10] [05:10] Sofia: Back on kernel/quantization — Priya, you recommended a kernel upgrade last week, what did we learn from the dry run?
[05:20] Priya: So the kernel upgrade (the new fp16 kernel + quant path) lowered p50 by ~6ms but introduced a tail regression in one of our tiny long-context models under 4k tokens due to a bug in KV eviction. We rolled it back on the test group and are tracking fix in the runtime repo. For Parkview we recommend a canary: upgrade 10% nodes, run full E2E, then escalate if no regressions in 24h. I added a rollback rehearsal section in the runbook.
[05:55] Liam: Can you run us through the rollback rehearsal? I want to make sure our infra team is ready to flip back if something goes sideways during core hours.
[06:03] Priya: Sure — steps are: 1) mark canary nodes, 2) drain traffic via NLB weight adjustments, 3) apply kernel package, 4) run warmup scripts that prime the KV with sample prompts, 5) monitor p95 and error rates for 30 minutes, 6) if regressions exceed thresholds revert image and reweight. The runbook has exact kubectl/cli snippets.
[06:30] Sofia: Those warmup scripts — do they rely on specific API keys or session ids? We want them to run from a CI job so they need reproducible tokens.
[06:40] Priya: We provide a short-lived token generator for test runs, the script uses that to create sessions and prime KV. We'll hand over the script.
[06:50] Rina: On telemetry we noticed a gap in request ID propagation through our ingress; sometimes the app-layer ID gets dropped at the NLB. Any recommendations?
[06:59] Priya: Put the request ID header in front and ensure X-Request-Id is preserved across LBs. Also ensure the NLB uses the preserveSourceIp flag and the app accepts forwarded headers; we have a snippet in the runbook.
[07:15] David: For audits, we require a full trace in case of an anomalous inference. Does Redwood store full token-level traces in the Private deployment by default?
[07:25] Priya: By default we store aggregated telemetry and sampling-level traces to limit exposure. For Private we can enable full trace retention in your VPC but it requires explicit config and retention S3 bucket with encryption supplied by your KMS. We documented the steps.
[07:45] Jordan: Quick commercial note — full-trace retention is an add-on due to storage costs; we'll put numbers in the appendix.
[07:52] Liam: Understood. Back to the canary and fallback: if the kernel upgrade causes a soft regression, what's our rollback RTO?
[07:59] Priya: In tests, rollback took ~7-12 minutes including reweighting and image redeploy. The majority of time is draining and warming the replacement nodes. That's why the rehearsal is important.
[08:15] Sofia: Can we shorten warmup by pre-warming cache on standby nodes?
[08:19] Priya: Yes, pre-warmed standby nodes are an option — you provision small reserved capacity on standby and we keep them primed; that increases baseline cost but reduces failover latency. Added that as an option in the config.
[08:35] Rina: On a different note, we had two failed runs where HTTP2 multiplexing caused head-of-line blocks. Is Redwood runtime sensitive to HTTP2?
[08:44] Priya: The runtime supports HTTP2 but for long running token streams we prefer simple HTTP/1 chunked streaming to avoid unexpected multiplexing behavior in some proxies. We put a flag in the client to prefer http1 for generator endpoints.
[08:58] Liam: Ok. Also curious about authentication: our preferred flow is mTLS + SAML SSO. Does the pilot support mTLS for backend-to-backend requests?
[09:08] Priya: Yes, mTLS is supported for private deployments; we can push down client certs at the NLB and validate in the gateway. The SAML SSO is for user console access. We'll include the cert rotation steps in the runbook.
[09:25] David: On encryption in transit, do you support TLS1.3 only?
[09:29] Priya: We prefer TLS1.3 and will negotiate that by default; TLS1.2 is available if you have legacy requirements, but it's opt-in.
[09:39] Jordan: We're about halfway through, quick check — any blockers on your side to proceed with the kernel canary next Tuesday?
[09:46] Sofia: We need the runbook updated with exact NLB settings and the sample warmup script. Also need confirmation that the runbook includes the egress ip mapping steps for the NAT scenario.
[09:56] Priya: I'll update both items and also add the sample terraform snippet for the NAT source preservation.
[10:03] Rina: We'll also need the smoke test curl commands for the readiness endpoint — put those in the runbook.
[10:08] Priya: Done, will add.
[10:11] [10:11] Jordan: Let's use the bench sheet as the source of truth for the surge test numbers. Priya, you mentioned a tail regression — is the fix in the runtime branch now?
[10:20] Priya: There's a PR open with the eviction fix; our runtime team ran it against the internal test suite and it passed. We'll plan to merge once Parkview gives the green light for a canary.
[10:30] Liam: Any chance of that PR introducing other changes we should be aware of?
[10:33] Priya: It's scoped to the KV eviction code path only, minimal other changes. We'll give you the PR link and a short changelog.
[10:39] Jordan: I'll put that in the follow-up email.
[10:42] Sofia: About monitoring, can you confirm which metrics will be forwarded to our Prometheus? Are we using push vs pull?
[10:48] Priya: For Private we expose a Prom endpoint inside your VPC; you can scrape it (pull) and we also push aggregated logs to your S3/bucket if you configure a sink. We'll add the Prom target snippet.
[11:00] Rina: Also, during the surge we saw a spike in out-of-memory logs tied to a mis-sized workspace. Are there recommended instance sizes for the mid-tier model?
[11:12] Priya: For your workload (avg 1k tokens, some 3k tails) we recommend a 48GB GPU node for mid-tier and a 80GB for long-context. We'll put a sizing table in the runbook.
[11:25] David: On compliance, can you supply the mapping of telemetry fields to SOC2 categories? Our auditor asked for a matrix.
[11:33] Jordan: We'll attach the matrix and the SOC2 certs in the follow-up.
[11:36] Liam: Good. A question about fallback economics: if we hit hosted fallback for 10% of p50 requests, what should we expect in cost delta?
[11:44] Jordan: We'll model that in the pricing appendix; ballpark it's a 7-10% increase depending on token mix and SSE of the model. We'll send a concrete calc for Parkview's v1 traffic.
[11:56] Priya: One more operational note — the runbook now includes a small playbook for debugging model regressions: how to collect sample prompts, how to run a local offline eval, and how to escalate to Redwood ML research.
[12:12] Sofia: Perfect.
[12:15] Rina: Quick scheduling — can we do the rehearsal window next Tue 2026-04-28 at 02:00 UTC? That's low-traffic for us.
[12:23] Jordan: Works for Redwood on our side. I'll put out a calendar invite.
[12:27] David: I'll loop in audit for a quick pre-check on the key policies.
[12:30] Jordan: Great. Any last questions?
[12:33] Liam: None from me, thanks.
[12:35] Jordan: To recap: Priya updates runbook + terraform NAT snippet and warmup scripts; Parkview runs egress IP smoke test and collects logs; Jordan sends pricing appendix and SOC2 matrix; schedule rehearsal for 2026-04-28. We'll reconvene on the normal weekly sync after the rehearsal.
[12:55] Priya: Thanks all.
[12:58] Sofia: thanks, bye.
[13:00] Meeting end.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-heard technical terms (N A T spelled out in notes), 'KV' sometimes written as 'K-V cash', 'quantization' appears as 'quantisization' in a few spots. Some speaker labels are human-provided and may be slightly off.
